recentItems.title: Beyond Borders Ep. 1 | The global divide: George Galloway & Zhao Hai
recentItems.description:
With global turbulence on the rise, friction between the Global North and the Global South is intensifying. Every day, we hear buzzwords like "sovereignty," "globalization," and "bloc politics." But what do they actually mean for our future? As China's Global Governance Initiative marks its first anniversary, the world is asking: What does good global governance really look like? In this episode, former British MP George Galloway sits down with Zhao Hai, director of international political studies at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences. Can this candid conversation between a veteran politician and a renowned scholar make sense of today's chaos? Let's find out.

recentItems.title: The Global North wants to contain China – but can't agree how
recentItems.description:
From the Global South to the Global North, is this divide about geography, ideology or the boundaries of a fading world order? As global power dynamics shift and no single force can define the future alone, blocs seeking unity through containing China are facing a difficult question: How long can such a strategy hold? In CGTN's Beyond Borders, former British MP George Galloway speaks with international affairs expert Zhao Hai on the identity crisis and strategic dilemmas of the Global North and why the dream of restoring the old order may never be realized.

recentItems.title: Money wasted on railway construction? Why the West doesn't understand China's governance system
recentItems.description:
Is China's railway construction "a waste of money" or an investment in the future? How should the value of a railway be measured? When some Western observers question China's large-scale infrastructure projects, they overlook the governance logic behind them. In CGTN's Beyond Borders, former British MP George Galloway talks with international affairs expert Zhao Hai to explore the different approaches to governance in China and the West. Why does China see infrastructure as a long-term development strategy, while some Western political systems are increasingly struggling to pursue long-term planning?

recentItems.title: Tajikistan's skills hub for young people
recentItems.description:
In Dushanbe, capital of Tajikistan, Central Asia's first Luban Workshop is employing advanced equipment and hands-on training to transform its students into sought-after technical professionals. The Luban Workshop is a key Shanghai Cooperation Organization initiative aimed at creating more opportunities for young people by promoting cooperation in education among its member states.

recentItems.title: Why reopening the rescue road to Gyirong Port is so challenging
recentItems.description:
More than 100 machines, steel-wire gabions and an increasingly complex operation: crews are racing to reopen the destroyed section of the G216 National Highway despite challenging conditions.

As the only road providing vehicle access to Gyirong Port from the Chinese side, restoring this vital rescue corridor remains a key part of operations following the mudslide that struck the China-Nepal border on August 26.
